L0: # WebGLRenderer
L1: 
L2: This renderer uses WebGL 2 to display scenes.
L3: 
L4: WebGL 1 is not supported since `r163`.
L5: 
L6: ## Constructor
L7: 
L8: ### new cite0†WebGLRenderer ( parameters : cite1†WebGLRenderer~Options )
L9: 
L10: Constructs a new WebGL renderer.
L11: 
L12: parameters  | The configuration parameter.
L13: 
L14: ## Properties
L15: 
L16: ### .cite2†autoClear : boolean
L17: 
L18: Whether the renderer should automatically clear its output before rendering a frame or not.
L19: 
L20: Default is `true`.
L21: ### .cite3†autoClearColor : boolean
L22: 
L23: If cite2†WebGLRenderer#autoClear set to `true`, whether the renderer should clear the color buffer or not.
L24: 
L25: Default is `true`.
L26: 
L27: ### .cite4†autoClearDepth : boolean
L28: 
L29: If cite2†WebGLRenderer#autoClear set to `true`, whether the renderer should clear the depth buffer or not.
L30: 
L31: Default is `true`.
L32: 
L33: ### .cite5†autoClearStencil : boolean
L34: 
L35: If cite2†WebGLRenderer#autoClear set to `true`, whether the renderer should clear the stencil buffer or not.
L36: 
L37: Default is `true`.
L38: ### .cite6†capabilities : cite7†WebGLRenderer~Capabilities L39: 
L40: Holds details about the capabilities of the current rendering context.
L41: 
L42: ### .cite8†clippingPlanes : Array.<cite9†Plane >
L43: 
L44: User-defined clipping planes specified in world space. These planes apply globally. Points in space whose dot product with the plane is negative are cut away.
L45: ### .cite10†coordinateSystem : cite11†WebGLCoordinateSystem | cite12†WebGPUCoordinateSystem (readonly)
L46: 
L47: Defines the coordinate system of the renderer.
L48: 
L49: In `WebGLRenderer`, the value is always `WebGLCoordinateSystem`.
L50: 
L51: Default is `WebGLCoordinateSystem`.
L52: ### .cite13†debug : Object
L53: 
L54: A object with debug configuration settings.
L55:   * `checkShaderErrors`: If it is `true`, defines whether material shader programs are checked for errors during compilation and linkage process. It may be useful to disable this check in production for performance gain. It is strongly recommended to keep these checks enabled during development. If the shader does not compile and link, it will not work and associated material will not render.
L56:   * `onShaderError(gl, program, glVertexShader,glFragmentShader)`: A callback function that can be used for custom error reporting. The callback receives the WebGL context, an instance of WebGLProgram as well two instances of WebGLShader representing the vertex and fragment shader. Assigning a custom function disables the default error reporting.
L57: ### .cite14†domElement : HTMLCanvasElement | OffscreenCanvas
L58: 
L59: A canvas where the renderer draws its output. This is automatically created by the renderer in the constructor (if not provided already); you just need to add it to your page like so:
L60: 
L61:     `document.body.appendChild( renderer.domElement );
L62:     `
L63: ### .cite15†extensions : Object
L64: 
L65: Provides methods for retrieving and testing WebGL extensions.
L66: 
L67:   * `get(extensionName:string)`: Used to check whether a WebGL extension is supported and return the extension object if available.
L68:   * `has(extensionName:string)`: returns `true` if the extension is supported.
L69: ### .cite16†info : cite17†WebGLRenderer~Info L70: 
L71: Holds a series of statistical information about the GPU memory and the rendering process. Useful for debugging and monitoring.
L72: 
L73: By default these data are reset at each render call but when having multiple render passes per frame (e.g. when using post processing) it can be preferred to reset with a custom pattern. First, set `autoReset` to `false`.
L74: 
L75:     `renderer.info.autoReset = false;
L76:     `
L77: Call `reset()` whenever you have finished to render a single frame.
L78: 
L79:     `renderer.info.reset();
L80:     `
L81: ### .cite18†isWebGLRenderer : boolean (readonly)
L82: 
L83: This flag can be used for type testing.
L84: 
L85: Default is `true`.
L86: 
L87: ### .cite19†localClippingEnabled : boolean
L88: 
L89: Whether the renderer respects object-level clipping planes or not.
L90: 
L91: Default is `false`.
L92: 
L93: ### .cite20†outputColorSpace : cite21†SRGBColorSpace | cite22†LinearSRGBColorSpace L94: 
L95: Defines the output color space of the renderer.
L96: 
L97: Default is `SRGBColorSpace`.
L98: 
L99: ### .cite23†properties : Object
L100: 
L101: Used to track properties of other objects like native WebGL objects.
L102: ### .cite24†renderLists : Object
L103: 
L104: Manages the render lists of the renderer.
L105: 
L106: ### .cite25†shadowMap : cite26†WebGLRenderer~ShadowMap L107: 
L108: Interface for managing shadows.
L109: ### .cite27†sortObjects : boolean
L110: 
L111: Whether the renderer should sort objects or not.
L112: 
L113: Note: Sorting is used to attempt to properly render objects that have some degree of transparency. By definition, sorting objects may not work in all cases. Depending on the needs of application, it may be necessary to turn off sorting and use other methods to deal with transparency rendering e.g. manually determining each object's rendering order.
L114: 
L115: Default is `true`.
L116: ### .cite28†state : Object
L117: 
L118: Interface for managing the WebGL state.
L119: 
L120: ### .cite29†toneMapping : cite30†NoToneMapping | cite31†LinearToneMapping | cite32†ReinhardToneMapping | cite33†CineonToneMapping | cite34†ACESFilmicToneMapping | cite35†CustomToneMapping | cite36†AgXToneMapping | cite37†NeutralToneMapping L121: 
L122: The tone mapping technique of the renderer.
L123: 
L124: Default is `NoToneMapping`.
L125: 
L126: ### .cite38†toneMappingExposure : number
L127: 
L128: Exposure level of tone mapping.
L129: 
L130: Default is `1`.
L131: ### .cite39†transmissionResolutionScale : number
L132: 
L133: The normalized resolution scale for the transmission render target, measured in percentage of viewport dimensions. Lowering this value can result in significant performance improvements when using cite40†MeshPhysicalMaterial#transmission .
L134: 
L135: Default is `1`.
L136: 
L137: ### .cite41†xr : cite42†WebXRManager L138: 
L139: A reference to the XR manager.

L141: ## Methods
L142: ### .cite43†clear ( color : boolean, depth : boolean, stencil : boolean )
L143: 
L144: Tells the renderer to clear its color, depth or stencil drawing buffer(s). This method initializes the buffers to the current clear color values.
L145: 
L146: color  | Whether the color buffer should be cleared or not. Default is `true`.
L147: depth  | Whether the depth buffer should be cleared or not. Default is `true`.
L148: stencil  | Whether the stencil buffer should be cleared or not. Default is `true`.
L149: ### .cite44†clearColor ()
L150: 
L151: Clears the color buffer. Equivalent to calling `renderer.clear( true, false, false )`.
L152: 
L153: ### .cite45†clearDepth ()
L154: 
L155: Clears the depth buffer. Equivalent to calling `renderer.clear( false, true, false )`.
L156: 
L157: ### .cite46†clearStencil ()
L158: 
L159: Clears the stencil buffer. Equivalent to calling `renderer.clear( false, false, true )`.
L160: ### .cite47†compile ( scene : cite48†Object3D , camera : cite49†Camera , targetScene : cite50†Scene ) : Set.<cite51†Material >
L161: 
L162: Compiles all materials in the scene with the camera. This is useful to precompile shaders before the first rendering. If you want to add a 3D object to an existing scene, use the third optional parameter for applying the target scene.
L163: 
L164: Note that the (target) scene's lighting and environment must be configured before calling this method.
L165: scene  | The scene or another type of 3D object to precompile.
L166: camera  | The camera.
L167: targetScene  | The target scene. Default is `null`.
L168: 
L169: Returns: The precompiled materials.
L170: ### .cite52†compileAsync ( scene : cite48†Object3D , camera : cite49†Camera , targetScene : cite50†Scene ) : Promise (async)
L171: 
L172: Asynchronous version of cite47†WebGLRenderer#compile .
L173: 
L174: This method makes use of the `KHR_parallel_shader_compile` WebGL extension. Hence, it is recommended to use this version of `compile()` whenever possible.
L175: 
L176: scene  | The scene or another type of 3D object to precompile.
L177: camera  | The camera.
L178: targetScene  | The target scene. Default is `null`.
L179: Returns: A Promise that resolves when the given scene can be rendered without unnecessary stalling due to shader compilation.
L180: ### .cite53†copyFramebufferToTexture ( texture : cite54†FramebufferTexture , position : cite55†Vector2 , level : number )
L181: 
L182: Copies pixels from the current bound framebuffer into the given texture.
L183: 
L184: texture  | The texture.
L185: position  | The start position of the copy operation. Default is `null`.
L186: level  | The mip level. The default represents the base mip. Default is `0`.
L187: ### .cite56†copyTextureToTexture ( srcTexture : cite57†Texture , dstTexture : cite57†Texture , srcRegion : cite58†Box2 | cite59†Box3 , dstPosition : cite55†Vector2 | cite60†Vector3 , srcLevel : number, dstLevel : number )
L188: 
L189: Copies data of the given source texture into a destination texture.
L190: 
L191: When using render target textures as `srcTexture` and `dstTexture`, you must make sure both render targets are initialized cite61†WebGLRenderer#initRenderTarget .
L192: srcTexture  | The source texture.
L193: dstTexture  | The destination texture.
L194: srcRegion  | A bounding box which describes the source region. Can be two or three-dimensional. Default is `null`.
L195: dstPosition  | A vector that represents the origin of the destination region. Can be two or three-dimensional. Default is `null`.
L196: srcLevel  | The source mipmap level to copy. Default is `0`.
L197: dstLevel  | The destination mipmap level. Default is `0`.
L198: ### .cite62†dispose ()
L199: 
L200: Frees the GPU-related resources allocated by this instance. Call this method whenever this instance is no longer used in your app.
L201: 
L202: ### .cite63†forceContextLoss ()
L203: 
L204: Simulates a loss of the WebGL context. This requires support for the `WEBGL_lose_context` extension.
L205: 
L206: ### .cite64†forceContextRestore ()
L207: 
L208: Simulates a restore of the WebGL context. This requires support for the `WEBGL_lose_context` extension.

L262:

L272: ### .cite77†getScissor ( target : cite78†Vector4 ) : cite78†Vector4 L273:

L281: 
L282: Returns `true` if the scissor test is enabled.
L283: 
L284: Returns: Whether the scissor test is enabled or not.
L285: ### .cite80†getSize ( target : cite55†Vector2 ) : cite55†Vector2 L286:

L300: ### .cite61†initRenderTarget ( target : cite76†WebGLRenderTarget )
L301: 
L302: Initializes the given WebGLRenderTarget memory. Useful for initializing a render target so data can be copied into it using cite56†WebGLRenderer#copyTextureToTexture before it has been rendered to.
L303: 
L304: target  | The render target.
L305: ### .cite82†initTexture ( texture : cite57†Texture )
L306: 
L307: Initializes the given texture. Useful for preloading a texture rather than waiting until first render (which can cause noticeable lags due to decode and GPU upload overhead).
L308: 
L309: texture  | The texture.
L310: ### .cite83†readRenderTargetPixels ( renderTarget : cite76†WebGLRenderTarget , x : number, y : number, width : number, height : number, buffer : TypedArray, activeCubeFaceIndex : number, textureIndex : number )
L311: 
L312: Reads the pixel data from the given render target into the given buffer.
L313: renderTarget  | The render target to read from.
L314: x  | The `x` coordinate of the copy region's origin.
L315: y  | The `y` coordinate of the copy region's origin.
L316: width  | The width of the copy region.
L317: height  | The height of the copy region.
L318: buffer  | The result buffer.
L319: activeCubeFaceIndex  | The active cube face index.
L320: textureIndex  | The texture index of an MRT render target. Default is `0`.
L321: ### .cite84†readRenderTargetPixelsAsync ( renderTarget : cite76†WebGLRenderTarget , x : number, y : number, width : number, height : number, buffer : TypedArray, activeCubeFaceIndex : number, textureIndex : number ) : Promise.<TypedArray> (async)
L322: 
L323: Asynchronous, non-blocking version of cite83†WebGLRenderer#readRenderTargetPixels .
L324: 
L325: It is recommended to use this version of `readRenderTargetPixels()` whenever possible.
L326: renderTarget  | The render target to read from.
L327: x  | The `x` coordinate of the copy region's origin.
L328: y  | The `y` coordinate of the copy region's origin.
L329: width  | The width of the copy region.
L330: height  | The height of the copy region.
L331: buffer  | The result buffer.
L332: activeCubeFaceIndex  | The active cube face index.
L333: textureIndex  | The texture index of an MRT render target. Default is `0`.
L334: 
L335: Returns: A Promise that resolves when the read has been finished. The resolve provides the read data as a typed array.
L336: ### .cite85†render ( scene : cite48†Object3D , camera : cite49†Camera )
L337: 
L338: Renders the given scene (or other type of 3D object) using the given camera.
L339: 
L340: The render is done to a previously specified render target set by calling cite86†WebGLRenderer#setRenderTarget or to the canvas as usual.
L341: By default render buffers are cleared before rendering but you can prevent this by setting the property `autoClear` to `false`. If you want to prevent only certain buffers being cleared you can `autoClearColor`, `autoClearDepth` or `autoClearStencil` to `false`. To force a clear, use cite43†WebGLRenderer#clear .
L342: 
L343: scene  | The scene to render.
L344: camera  | The camera.
L345: ### .cite87†resetState ()
L346: 
L347: Can be used to reset the internal WebGL state. This method is mostly relevant for applications which share a single WebGL context across multiple WebGL libraries.
L348: 
L349: ### .cite88†setAnimationLoop ( callback : cite89†onAnimationCallback )
L350: 
L351: Applications are advised to always define the animation loop with this method and not manually with `requestAnimationFrame()` for best compatibility.
L352: 
L353: callback  | The application's animation loop.
L354: ### .cite90†setClearAlpha ( alpha : number )
L355: 
L356: Sets the clear alpha.
L357: 
L358: alpha  | The clear alpha.
L359: 
L360: ### .cite91†setClearColor ( color : cite69†Color , alpha : number )
L361: 
L362: Sets the clear color and alpha.
L363: 
L364: color  | The clear color.
L365: alpha  | The clear alpha. Default is `1`.
L366: ### .cite92†setDrawingBufferSize ( width : number, height : number, pixelRatio : number )
L367: 
L368: This method allows to define the drawing buffer size by specifying width, height and pixel ratio all at once. The size of the drawing buffer is computed with this formula:
L369: 
L370:     `size.x = width * pixelRatio;
L371:     size.y = height * pixelRatio;
L372:     `
L373: 
L374: width  | The width in logical pixels.
L375: height  | The height in logical pixels.
L376: pixelRatio  | The pixel ratio.
L377: ### .cite93†setEffects ( effects : Array )
L378: 
L379: Sets the post-processing effects to be applied after rendering.
L380: 
L381: effects  | An array of post-processing effects.
L382: 
L383: ### .cite94†setNodesHandler ( nodesHandler : cite95†WebGLNodesHandler )
L384: 
L385: Sets a compatibility node builder for rendering node materials with WebGLRenderer. This enables using TSL (Three.js Shading Language) node materials to prepare for migration to WebGPURenderer.
L386: 
L387: nodesHandler  | The node builder instance.
L388: ### .cite96†setOpaqueSort ( method : function )
L389: 
L390: Sets a custom opaque sort function for the render lists. Pass `null` to use the default `painterSortStable` function.
L391: 
L392: method  | The opaque sort function.
L393: 
L394: ### .cite97†setPixelRatio ( value : number )
L395: 
L396: Sets the given pixel ratio and resizes the canvas if necessary.
L397: 
L398: value  | The pixel ratio.
L399: ### .cite86†setRenderTarget ( renderTarget : cite76†WebGLRenderTarget , activeCubeFace : number, activeMipmapLevel : number )
L400: 
L401: Sets the active rendertarget.
L402: 
L403: renderTarget  | The render target to set. When `null` is given, the canvas is set as the active render target instead.
L404: activeCubeFace  | The active cube face when using a cube render target. Indicates the z layer to render in to when using 3D or array render targets. Default is `0`.
L405: activeMipmapLevel  | The active mipmap level. Default is `0`.
L406: ### .cite98†setScissor ( x : number | cite78†Vector4 , y : number, width : number, height : number )
L407: 
L408: Sets the scissor region to render from `(x, y)` to `(x + width, y + height)`.
L409: x  | The horizontal coordinate for the lower left corner of the scissor region origin in logical pixel unit. Or alternatively a four-component vector specifying all the parameters of the scissor region.
L410: y  | The vertical coordinate for the lower left corner of the scissor region origin in logical pixel unit.
L411: width  | The width of the scissor region in logical pixel unit.
L412: height  | The height of the scissor region in logical pixel unit.
L413: ### .cite99†setScissorTest ( boolean : boolean )
L414: 
L415: Enable or disable the scissor test. When this is enabled, only the pixels within the defined scissor area will be affected by further renderer actions.
L416: 
L417: boolean  | Whether the scissor test is enabled or not.
L418: ### .cite100†setSize ( width : number, height : number, updateStyle : boolean )
L419: 
L420: Resizes the output canvas to (width, height) with device pixel ratio taken into account, and also sets the viewport to fit that size, starting in (0, 0). Setting `updateStyle` to false prevents any style changes to the output canvas.
L421: 
L422: width  | The width in logical pixels.
L423: height  | The height in logical pixels.
L424: updateStyle  | Whether to update the `style` attribute of the canvas or not. Default is `true`.
L425: ### .cite101†setTransparentSort ( method : function )
L426: 
L427: Sets a custom transparent sort function for the render lists. Pass `null` to use the default `reversePainterSortStable` function.
L428: 
L429: method  | The opaque sort function.
L430: ### .cite102†setViewport ( x : number | cite78†Vector4 , y : number, width : number, height : number )
L431: 
L432: Sets the viewport to render from `(x, y)` to `(x + width, y + height)`.
L433: x  | The horizontal coordinate for the lower left corner of the viewport origin in logical pixel unit. Or alternatively a four-component vector specifying all the parameters of the viewport.
L434: y  | The vertical coordinate for the lower left corner of the viewport origin in logical pixel unit.

L2: # BufferGeometry
L3: 
L4: A representation of mesh, line, or point geometry. Includes vertex positions, face indices, normals, colors, UVs, and custom attributes within buffers, reducing the cost of passing all this data to the GPU.
L5: ## Code Example
L6: 
L7:     `const geometry = new THREE.BufferGeometry();
L8:     // create a simple square shape. We duplicate the top left and bottom right
L9:     // vertices because each vertex needs to appear once per triangle.
L10:     const vertices = new Float32Array( [
L11:     	-1.0, -1.0,  1.0, // v0
L12:     	 1.0, -1.0,  1.0, // v1
L13:     	 1.0,  1.0,  1.0, // v2
L14:     	 1.0,  1.0,  1.0, // v3
L15:     	-1.0,  1.0,  1.0, // v4
L16:     	-1.0, -1.0,  1.0  // v5
L17:     ] );
L18:     // itemSize = 3 because there are 3 values (components) per vertex
L19:     geometry.setAttribute( 'position', new THREE.BufferAttribute( vertices, 3 ) );
L20:     const material = new THREE.MeshBasicMaterial( { color: 0xff0000 } );
L21:     const mesh = new THREE.Mesh( geometry, material );
L22:     `
